subject.title: config: use datetime suffix for config backup files instead of numeric rotation

question: Should the timestamped backup migration preserve or convert existing numbered `.bak.N` recovery points, or may first-run cleanup delete them?
rationale: Config backups are user recovery data and may contain sensitive config content, so deleting or no longer hardening legacy backup files is a compatibility and security-boundary choice that should be explicit before merge.

options.title: Preserve or convert legacy backups
options.body: Require this PR or a replacement to keep existing `.bak.N` recovery points, include them in chmod hardening, and migrate/prune them only after equivalent timestamped retention exists.

options.title: Accept timestamp-only cleanup
options.body: Allow first-run cleanup to delete existing numbered backups, but document the upgrade behavior and explicitly accept the recovery-point loss.

options.title: Keep numeric backups for now
options.body: Reject or pause the timestamped naming change and keep the documented numbered ring until a safer migration plan is sponsored.

recommendation.title: Preserve or convert legacy backups
recommendation.body: Require this PR or a replacement to keep existing `.bak.N` recovery points, include them in chmod hardening, and migrate/prune them only after equivalent timestamped retention exists.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent config recovery and backup-test history among the likely owners and is best positioned to decide upgrade-safety policy.
